title: One object instead of a choice of vacuum to put the observer in de Sitter space: From wormholes, black holes and baby universes to the criteria for an observer in de Sitter, contrasted with the Kaluza–Klein graviton candidates and with the cosmological constant
description: In de Sitter space an observer must be inside the universe it observes, and in string theory placing it has become a choice: of a vacuum among some 10^500. The same choice returns where wormholes, black holes and baby universes meet. The baby universes that branch off through wormholes carry parameters that fix the constants of nature, the cosmological constant among them, and the same parameters label the boundary theories over which the gravity of a black-hole throat is averaged; in both the question is which value, and the answer is sought in what a throat contains. The programme to which this note belongs, written within critical realism, reads the difficulty as one of representation rather than of selection: what is missing is one object that meets the criteria Witten and Chandrasekaran, Longo, Penington and Witten set for an observer in de Sitter, not a choice among values. This note does not test that claim itself; it tests two of its consequences where data can reach them, on the particles of one throat and on the cosmological constant. The object, in the framework of the programme, is a microstate whose levels form a tower built from two numbers, π and the golden ratio φ; read as a warped extra dimension it is a throat, the golden throat, whose Kaluza–Klein modes are its particles. The question becomes whether the tower fixes what a throat model otherwise chooses. The two-brane model of Randall and Sundrum assumes the dimension and chooses the infrared scale and the depth. The golden throat has the same equations, so the same mass ratios, and four independent conditions of the tower, reflection positivity, four-dimensional gravity, the arity of the framework and the clock of φ, fix its spectrum with no free parameter, to leading order π(k+1/4) times Mφ^12 in the unit M of the framework. The arity gives the dimension that the two-brane model assumes; with M identified with the scale of the charged leptons and the level 12 with the bottom of the throat, the spectrum fixes the infrared scale that it chooses. Identified with the graviton candidates reported at 380 and 700 GeV, they place the bottom of the throat at 11.97±0.05, 0.6 standard deviations from 12, and give the next modes at 1028 and 1346 GeV, against 1014 and 1328 GeV for the two-brane model fitted to the same candidates. Only the depth, the position of the top, stays free, and the ratio of the vector modes can decide it if they share the throat. The same tower carries the observer of de Sitter space. In the gravitational unit of the framework the observed cosmological constant gives the observer's level, 583.79±0.03: the level is read from the data, not chosen, and the hypothesis that it sits at an integer level is excluded within ΛCDM at 7.6 standard deviations. What the note leaves open is one number, the ratio of the lepton scale to the Planck scale.
